subject: Different Behavior of Local Backend and Hadoop Backend?

messages.author: 03290ff051991093
messages.subject: Different Behavior of Local Backend and Hadoop Backend?
parts:
Hi,

I noticed that the local backend and the Hadoop backend seem to behave differently (I'll explain exactly what I mean further below). I'm not sure whether this is a bug or a feature, or whether I'm misunderstanding something.

When I use Hadoop as the backend, the mapper gets for example
k is c(1,1,1,2,2,2)
v is c(8,6,4,7,3,6)

When I use the local backend, the mapper first gets
k is 1
v is c(8,6,4)
and then the mapper gets called again with
k is 2
v is c(7,3,6)

Instead, I would have thought that the mapper with the local backend should get
k is c(1,1,1)
v is c(8,6,4)
and then the mapper should get called again with
k is c(2,2,2)
v is c(7,3,6)

I am mentioning this, since this behavior means I would have to write the mapper differently for the local backend compared to the Hadoop backend. Effectively, I would have to manually do some recycling to first convert 1 to c(1,1,1) before I could run the same code on the local backend and the Hadoop backend. This is quite cumbersome, in particular since the local backend should be usable for debugging. But again, maybe I'm misunderstanding something.

Thanks,
M
